records.activity: A class of fishermen being taught special features of the internal combustion engine by their teacher at Anstruther.

te.text:
FISHERMEN GO TO SCHOOL.

With the fishing industry nowadays mostly pursued
by steam drifters and modern motor vessels, fishermen,
following the modern desire for knowledge, have gone
back to school determined to know as much about the
technical side of their work as they do the practical.
During the present off-season a large number of fishermen
are attending special twice weekly classes at the Waid
Academy, Anstruther, Fife, where they are studying the
construction and working of modern engines and their operation.

Photo shows:- A class of fishermen being taught special
features of the internal combustion engine by their teacher
at Anstruther.
Fox January 2nd. 39.

records.activity: the last yards of a 16-mile length of submarine power cable being coiled in a specially constructed shed at a factory

te.text:
138,000 VOLT SUBMARINE POWER CABLE FOR VANCOUVER.

At their Trafford Park, Manchester, factory, British
Insulated Callender's (Submarine Cables) Ltd., have
completed the first stage of an order valued at over
three-million dollars, for the supply and installation
of 138,000-volt submarine cable for the British Columbia
Electric Company of Canada, who are linking their high-
voltage system in the southern part of Vancouver Island
with the unlimited hydro-electric resources on the mainland
of British Columbia. The cable system consists of single core
cables, each 16 miles in length, with similar cables 3 1/2 miles
long for the inter-island section. At four inches diameter and
weighing 50lbs a yard, this will be the largest continuous
long-length power cable ever installed. Special loading and
transport arrangements are necessary for cable of this size
and weight and a special Coiling Down Shed has been constructed
for it's storage.

PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS: The last yards of a 16-mile length of
cable being coiled on one of the huge cable stacks in the
specially constructed coiling down shed at the Trafford Park,
Manchester, factory of British Insulated Callender's (Submarine
Cables), Ltd. who have manufactured it for the British
Columbia Electric Company.

FOX PHOTOS MAY 2ND. 1956 32623

A PRESS VISIT TO THE TRAFFORD PARK, MANCHESTER, FACTORY
OF BRITISH INSULATED CALLENDER'S CABLES, LTD. HAS BEEN
ARRANGED FOR TODAY.
File: Industry - Fuel & Power - Electricity - Cable Making

records.activity: Looking along the keel of a new ship at the yards

te.text:
BRITAIN'S SHIPYARDS ARE WINNING AGAINST THE U-BOATS.   Y
Despite the savage U-boat warfare on our merchant vessels,
figures since the outbreak of war show that our shipbuilding
industry is more than making up for losses incurred.  New
ships, captures and conversions have given our Mercantile
Marine more tonnage than ever - although thousands of tons
of shipping has been sent to the bottom of the seas.  The
Mercantile Marine has mobilised and ships are being turned
out at an amazing rate.  These pictures, from " Somewhere in
England " confirm the fact that Britain's shipyards are
winning against the efforts of enemy submarine warfare.

Photo shows-  Birth of a ship.  Looking along the keel of
a new ship at the yards.  In a week or so the ribs will be
rapidly taking shape, reaching up to the sky.
Fox Nov 22nd. 39.  PASSED BY CENSOR.  ( 233608 ).

te.text:
FOR FIRST PUBLICATION

SPINNING THE ARTERIES OF OUR CIVILISATION.
61.. 141.
This is one of a remarkable new series of photo-
graphs taken mainly by the natural light of the
process by which a British ironworks produces
mile upon mile of cast iron pipes for the public
services of gas [illegible] and water which are a prime
necessity of civilised life. A large percentage
of these pipes are spun by a centrifugal process
which eliminates defects and gives a close-grained
metal, easily worked and with a high degree of
resilience and resistance to impact. In addition
to its own requirements, the plant also produces
pig-iron for steel manufacture, contributing largely
therefore to the country's output of armaments.
An impressive scene at the furnace. Pouring molten
iron into the hopper for the centrifugal casting
of pipes for gas, water and sewage, etc.,
The pipe so produced is as a "spun" pipe.

EXCLUSIVE
CENTRAL PRESS PHOTO
MADE IN ENGLAND

CERTIFIED BY
CENTRAL PRESS
PHOTOS, LTD.

"IT'S A CARVE UP" 
 WOOD CARVERS WORK IN OLD SOUTHWARK PRISON 
 DG/HT 
 Busy in the watch room of the old King's Bench 
 prison ( where Smollet served a term, and 
 Dickens placed Micawber) wood carvers are

 main buildings were demolished in 1869 and 
 the firm of E. J. Bradford stone and wood 
 carvers occupy the watch room .

 old King's Bench Prison, Southwark.

records.activity: shipyard workers returning to work, seen against the giant hull of a merchant vessel in the stocks

te.text:
BUILDING SHIPS FOR THE MERCHANT NAVY.	E.M./MCN.

British shipyards are launching merchant vessels with
all possible speed; a 10,000 tonner now gets its last
coat of paint only 5½ months after the keel-laying.
Widespread use of pre-fabrication has helped this speed-
up and welding instead of rivetting has saved time and
steel. This series of pictures taken at a shipyard
shows ships in various stages of completion in the stocks.
At the present rate of progress it will not be long
before these same ships are on active service for Britain.

Photo shows:-  Shipyard workers returning to work are
dwarfed by the giant hull of one of our new ships in
stocks.
